key_decisions.decision: Keep Bilhah’s enslaved status, the sexual arrangement, the knees ritual image, and Rachel’s building-family language; add no consent.
Preserve both wife status and enslavement, and render the sexual euphemism directly without implying Bilhah chose the arrangement.
Render dananni as favorable judgment while keeping Rachel’s claim to the child and the Dan wordplay in her voice.
Render struggles-of-God as an intensifier without claiming the struggle was divinely commanded; retain rivalry and name wordplay.
Keep Leah’s motive, Zilpah’s enslavement, and the imposed wife status parallel to Bilhah.
Follow the recorded traditional reading, two words meaning good fortune has come, and retain the Gad wordplay.
Keep Leah’s accusation and Rachel’s bargaining over Jacob’s sexual access as their speech; identify Jacob without endorsing ownership.
Render the emphatic hire language and obligatory claim plainly while leaving the arrangement’s troubling agency visible.
Keep Leah’s interpretation, slave woman, and wages/name wordplay as her claim rather than the narrator’s judgment.
Choose honor for the difficult name-related verb while retaining gift, hope, six sons, and Leah’s own interpretation.
Retain the add/Joseph wordplay and Rachel’s forward-looking petition alongside verse 23’s take-away association.
Preserve the troubling labor-for-wives construction as Jacob’s contractual claim, with wives and children as people rather than wages.
Retain Laban’s admitted divination and attribution to the LORD without validating the practice or replacing it with mere observation.
Preserve the species/color categories while using animal where Hebrew seh can encompass sheep or goats; identify the marked future wage.
Identify Laban as the ambiguous subject from the sons and ensuing separation; preserve every marked category and his action before future breeding.
Retain the three tree types provisionally and the physical stripping/exposure process without modern genetic explanation.
Report the narrative sequence without claiming the branches scientifically caused the offspring’s markings.
Follow the difficult herd-management description while retaining separation, visual orientation, and distinct ownership.
